claude.performance_metric: net revenues grew from $18.8bn (2013) to $28.2bn (2017); standalone reporting company retained
claude.rationale: On the product/operations interface, the slice documents no realized incoherence: AbbVie grew net revenues each year and successfully absorbed a bolt-on (Pharmacyclics, ~$20.8bn) into its operating base, with the only product risk being HUMIRA concentration and patent expiry—not a product-vs-process misalignment (p4=0). On the operations/organization interface, headcount stayed near closing levels (~29,000 vs ~30,000 expected) and separation costs were recognized as an ordinary standalone build-out ($265m in 2015 SG&A) with no documented fracture between operations and people/management/culture (p5=0). The record describes an independent separation that operated as intended with no archetype incoherence (t1=0) and a single, coherent pharmaceutical value-capture model (t2=0).

gemini.rationale: The slice documents AbbVie's successful operation as a standalone entity with growing revenues and stable headcount. There is no evidence of product/process disruption (p4_pathway = 0) or process/organization fracture (p5_pathway = 0) over the 3-5 year horizon.

grok.rationale: The slice documents continued concentration in HUMIRA (~65% of 2017 revenue) and a bolt-on acquisition (Pharmacyclics) with rising revenues, and does not document any product/process alignment failure, so p4_pathway=0. Headcount stayed comparable (~29k vs ~30k expected) with only ordinary post-separation SG&A costs noted and no operations-vs-organization fracture, so p5_pathway=0.
